title: [#305/#322][#303][#297] Retain the current tuning in the Tuner trait and restore it on reset
body:
## Summary

Turning an output device off and on again (e.g. a digital piano turned off overnight) left it in 12-EDO. `TrackManager` resets the track's tuner on `MidiDeviceOpenedEvent`, but `Tuner.reset()` did not restate the current tuning: MTS tuners did not keep the tuning at all, and the Monophonic Pitch Bend tuner kept it but zeroed the tuning pitch bend of C, so the first C played after a reset was untuned.

Sub-issue of #305: this applies only the `Tuner` shape change described there.

- `Tuner.tune` and `Tuner.reset` are now `final`. `tune` stores the tuning in the trait, exposed through a public `tuning` accessor, and delegates to the new abstract `onTune`. `reset` delegates to the new `onReset`, then restates the current tuning through `onTune`.
- `MtsTuner`, `MonophonicPitchBendTuner` and `MpeTuner` implement `onTune` / `onReset`, tuning to the tuning `onTune` receives. `MpeTuner` and `MonophonicPitchBendTuner` drop their own tuning field: `MonophonicPitchBendTuner.onTune` derives the tuning pitch bend of the last note from the tuning it gets and marks it for sending only when it changed, so zeroing it on reset is enough for `onTune` to rebuild it.
- `tune` stores the tuning only once `onTune` returns, so a tuning a tuner fails to apply (e.g. beyond its Pitch Bend Sensitivity) leaves the current one in place instead of breaking every later reset. The stacked follow-up #327 replaces this with `Tuner.canTune` and clamping.
- A reset now stops what the output device plays before clearing the state that tracks it, and returns the device to the state the tuner then assumes. Both tuners release the pedals listed in the shared `Tuner.NoteHoldingPedals` (Sustain and Sostenuto).
  - `MonophonicPitchBendTuner` sends a Note Off for the note sounding, releases the pedals left down, and resets the Pitch Bend to 0 before configuring the Pitch Bend Sensitivity.
  - `MpeTuner`, which already sent the Note Offs, returns the pedals, then the Pitch Bend, it forwarded to a Master Channel to their defaults, releasing the pedals of every input channel first so that the notes they hold stop before their pitch changes. It also returns `CC #74` and Channel Pressure to their defaults on each Member Channel where the allocators record another value, before restating the configured Zones. It resets only what it sent itself, not what another source left on the output device. A Member Channel's Pitch Bend, sent ahead of every note allocated there, is reset only on a Member Channel that the restated Zones turn into a Master Channel, where it would bend every note of the Zone.
- The `TODO #305` comments in `TrackManager` that this addresses are removed, and the ScalaDocs and architecture docs are updated, describing a reset as (re)configuring the output device.

This builds on the first attempt, e22d0b3, which kept the tuning on reset in `MpeTuner` and `MonophonicPitchBendTuner` only.

## Startup

The app still starts in the first tuning (index 0). Tracks are built before the tunings are loaded, so each tuner reset restates 12-EDO (for an MTS tuner that is one 12-EDO SysEx when its track is built), and loading the tunings then tunes every track to the one at index 0. An output device that opens after the tunings are loaded now keeps that tuning instead of dropping to 12-EDO.

## Not in this PR (remaining in #305)

- `TunerProcessor.onDetach` and `Track.close()` still send the courtesy 12-EDO messages through `tune(Tuning.Standard)`, which also makes 12-EDO the tuner's current tuning (`TODO #305`). The read-only 12-EDO method planned in #305 replaces that.
- A tuner is not yet reset when its output is detached, which the `MpeTuner` reset now assumes: it resets only the Member Channel values it sent itself, so a tuner that preceded it on the same output (e.g. before a tracks file was loaded) may leave values behind (`TODO #305`).
- `reset` still re-applies the configuration passed to the constructor (e.g. the MPE Zones and input mode) rather than the runtime one.
- Rebuilding the tracks (`TrackManager.replaceAllTracks`, e.g. after editing them) does not tune the new tracks to the current tuning, as before: they play in 12-EDO until the next tuning change.

## Tests

- `TunerTest` covers the new `Tuner` contract through a shared `FakeTuner` test double, which also replaces the ScalaMock `Tuner` stubs in `TrackTest` and `TunerProcessorTest`, since ScalaMock cannot stub `final` methods. It also covers a tuner keeping its current tuning when it fails to apply a new one, and restating it on reset.
- Reset tests for each tuner, including the C regression of the Monophonic Pitch Bend tuner, and the note, pedals and Pitch Bend a reset during playing must not leave behind, for `MonophonicPitchBendTuner` and, in both input modes, `MpeTuner`: the pedals released before the Pitch Bend, the Member Channel resets for the values it left and those it did not, for both Zones, for Zones an MCM changed before the reset, and the Pitch Bend of a Member Channel that the restated Zones turn into the Master Channel of the Lower or the Upper Zone.
- `TrackManagerTest`: the current tuning is restored when the output device reopens, when the devices are turned off and on again, and after the input device is gone; the first tuning is kept at startup, also when the output device opens after the tunings are loaded.
- The full test suite passes. `tuner` coverage: 89.98% statements, 87.07% branches; the changed methods are fully covered.

Resolves #303
Resolves #322
Resolves #297
